file_insights.changes_summary: Refactored warehouse_list view function to use apply_list_filters utility instead of manual filtering and pagination
key_modifications: Replaced manual search filtering with FilterConfig
Removed manual pagination logic in favor of apply_list_filters
Preserved queryset annotations for statistics (total_materials, total_stock_quantity)
Simplified context building by using result dictionary from apply_list_filters

patterns_discovered.description: Migration from inline filtering logic to centralized apply_list_filters utility
patterns_discovered.benefit: Reduces code duplication and improves maintainability across views

patterns_discovered.description: Base queryset with annotations is separated from filter application
patterns_discovered.benefit: Allows clean separation of concerns - statistics calculation independent of filtering

patterns_discovered.description: FilterConfig objects define filtering behavior declaratively
patterns_discovered.benefit: Makes filtering rules explicit and reusable across different views

patterns_discovered.description: apply_list_filters returns structured dictionary with queryset and filter_values
patterns_discovered.benefit: Consistent interface for accessing paginated results and applied filter values

gotchas_discovered.description: Search value must be extracted from result['filter_values'] dictionary instead of direct request parameter
gotchas_discovered.impact: Template context now receives 'search' from filter_values, ensuring consistency with applied filters
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Using result['filter_values'].get('search', '') with fallback ensures backward compatibility

gotchas_discovered.description: Manual .order_by('code') was removed from queryset chain and moved to default_ordering parameter
gotchas_discovered.impact: Default ordering is now applied by apply_list_filters utility rather than in queryset definition
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Specified default_ordering='code' parameter to maintain consistent sort behavior

gotchas_discovered.description: apply_list_filters returns result object instead of paginated queryset directly
gotchas_discovered.impact: Must access paginated queryset via result['queryset'] and filter values via result['filter_values']
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Documentation or type hints needed to clarify result dictionary structure

approach_outcome.description: Successfully refactored warehouse_list view to use apply_list_filters utility
approach_outcome.completeness: Complete refactoring achieved on first attempt
code_quality_improvements: Reduced view function from 32 lines to 25 lines (22% reduction)
Eliminated manual pagination and filtering code
Improved consistency with other refactored views using same utility
Maintained functional equivalence - same search fields and pagination behavior

recommendations.recommendation: Verify that all other list views in inventory app follow the same apply_list_filters pattern
Add type hints or docstring documenting apply_list_filters return value structure (queryset, filter_values, pagination_info)
Ensure warehouse_list.html template is using result['filter_values']['search'] correctly if it references the search context variable
Add integration tests to verify search filtering, pagination, and annotation statistics all work correctly together
Continue applying this pattern to remaining list views that have manual filtering/pagination logic
